title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): L is a totally ordered set (the 'line'). M = M_0 ∪ M_1 is the set of cells of a finite subdivision. M_0 consists of the points P_a (a∈L), identified with L. M_1 consists of the segments S_ab (a<b). M is ordered by the face relation P_a ≤ S_ab, P_b ≤ S_ab. A 'polyfigure' Φ is an arbitrary subset of M. A 'figure' is a closed (downward-closed) subset. Drap(L) denotes the finite subsets ('flags') of L. On the previous page convex polyfigures were classified by pairs (T, α): T is a flag, F_T is the closed subdivided interval with vertex set T, α ⊂ ∂T is the set of removed endpoints, and Φ = F_T \ α. This gives closed, half-open and open segments.

This page sets up three combinatorial invariants of a polyfigure Φ.
(1) The closure F = Φ̄, i.e. the down-closure for ≤.
(2) The vertex set δΦ := δF = F ∩ M_0 = {a | ∃X∈Φ, P_a ≤ X}. This is a flag. It is empty iff Φ is empty, and it has one element iff Φ = {P_a}. A margin warning notes that a vertex a need not satisfy P_a ∈ Φ, e.g. Φ = {S_ab}.
(3) For convex Φ, the boundary ∂Φ := ∂F. It is ∅ if card δΦ ≤ 1. Otherwise it is {min δΦ, max δΦ}, so ∂Φ is ∅ or a 2-element flag.

Also for convex Φ, a set Φ· (the 'extremal/special points'): it equals ∂Φ if card δΦ ≥ 2, {a} if Φ = {P_a}, and ∅ if Φ = ∅.

For general Φ, both ∂ and · are extended additively over the convex components Φ_i: ∂Φ = ∪∂Φ_i and Φ· = ∪Φ_i·.

Worked example: Φ = {S_ab, S_bc, P_d} with a<b<c<d. The convex components are S_ab, S_bc and P_d, because P_b is missing so the two open segments are separate components. This gives δΦ = {a,b,c,d}, ∂Φ = {a,b,c} and Φ· = {a,b,c,d}.

Margin notes sketch an alternative, local definition via a valence. For a point a, ordre_a(Ψ) = #{X ∈ M_1 ∩ Ψ | a is a vertex of X}. The cases are:
- 0: an exterior point, or an isolated point if P_a ∈ Ψ;
- 1: a boundary point;
- 2: an interior point, or a 'frontier' point if P_a ∉ Ψ (a puncture between two segments).

The next page proves ∂Φ ⊂ Φ· ⊂ δΦ and Φ· = ∂Φ ⊔ Φ_isol. It then introduces a positional order <_pos on M.

Purpose: an elementary, purely order-theoretic dévissage of one-dimensional 'tame' figures. These are finite unions of points and open segments in an ordered line, serving as the base case of the 1986 'Analysis situs' project.
errors: The component-wise ∂ and the margin's valence-based notion do not agree. In the example, b has valence 2 and P_b ∉ Φ, so it is a 'frontier' rather than a 'bord' point; yet b ∈ ∂Φ under the union definition. The valence definition would give ∂ = {a,c}. Grothendieck seems aware of this, since the margin distinguishes 'point frontière', but the two definitions are left unreconciled on this page.

For non-convex Φ the 'boundary' ∂Φ = ∪∂Φ_i is not the topological boundary of Φ in any usual sense. It includes, for instance, points of Φ where two closed pieces meet only if they lie in different components. This is a definitional choice, not an error, but the name may mislead.
The ∂ characterization on the next page carries a caveat about the existence of a largest or smallest element of L. That caveat is not reflected here, but this is harmless for finite flags.

ideas.what: Polyfigures as arbitrary subsets of the face poset of a subdivided ordered line, with closure as down-closure.
ideas.modern_name: Open/closed subsets of a finite poset (Alexandrov topology); constructible subsets of a 1-dim cell complex

ideas.what: Classification of convex figures as (flag T, subset of endpoints removed): closed, half-open and open segments.
ideas.modern_name: Intervals / 1-cells in o-minimal or semilinear cell decomposition
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme (1984).

ideas.what: Invariants δΦ (vertex set), ∂Φ (union of endpoints of convex components) and Φ· (∂Φ plus isolated points), with ∂Φ ⊂ Φ· ⊂ δΦ.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial boundary / vertex set of a 1-dim constructible set

ideas.what: Local valence ordre_a(Ψ) = number of 1-cells of Ψ incident to a, used to classify points as exterior, isolated, boundary, interior or frontier.
ideas.modern_name: Vertex degree / local link type in a graph; local Euler characteristic data

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but elementary bookkeeping of the combinatorics of points and segments on an ordered line. It is historically interesting as part of Grothendieck's 1986 tame-topology foundations, but it contains no result or connection unknown to specialists.
transcription_corrections: The NB reads 'δΦ = δF ∈ Drap*(L)' (flags, possibly empty); the crossed-out text is about 'sommets/points extrêmes de la polyfigure Φ'.
The first margin note reads approximately: 'Attention, si a est un sommet de Φ, on n'a pas nécessairement P_a ∈ Φ, ex: Φ = {S_ab}'.
The bottom-left margin defines ordre_a(Ψ) = card({X ∈ M_1 ∩ Ψ | a ∈ δX}) (vertex incidence), for Ψ ⊂ M and a ∈ L.
The struck-out first definition reads '∂Φ = ∂F = {∅ si card δF ≤ 1; ...}' with 'extrémités de δF' — consistent with the transcription.
